U.K. energy bill proposes changes to waste transport regulation

November 6, 2026, 12:11 pmNuclear News

A bill introduced in the U.K. Parliament on November 4 includes a provision that potentially would streamline the government’s process for updating rules regarding the transportation of used fuel and radioactive waste.

Contained within the Energy Independence Bill are measures that would affect several sectors of the United Kingdom’s energy system in what would amount to a major overhaul. Among the proposals that the legislation calls for are measures to accelerate the deployment of what it identifies as “clean energy” projects, including offshore wind and smart grid projects; support for insulating and otherwise updating residential buildings under the Warm Homes Plan; and an end to licenses for new oil and natural gas exploration.

Thea Energy, MIT collaborate on testing stellarator magnet technology

November 6, 2026, 10:13 amNuclear News
Concept art showing Thea Energy’s Eos stellarator design. (Image: Thea Energy)

Stellarator developer Thea Energy has announced that it is collaborating with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology on the testing and validation of an encircling magnet coil for the fusion firm’s Eos stellarator. The work will take place at MIT’s Plasma Science and Fusion Center (PSFC) in Cambridge, Mass.

Korean companies partner with U.S. start-ups

November 6, 2026, 7:18 amNuclear News

In recent months, much attention has been paid to the deal between the United States and South Korea involving the potential construction of eight new gigawatt-scale reactors. Outside of that spotlight, however, significant U.S.-Korean collaboration continues on the small reactor front.

In the past two weeks, Elementl Power partnered with DS Investment Partners and Hyundai partnered with ARC Clean Technology, Nano Nuclear, and First American Nuclear.
